newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VALENCIA, BARCELONA HIT BY WORLD CUP ABSENTEES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VALENCIA, BARCELONA HIT BY WORLD CUP ABSENTEES.

text.p: Valencia and Barcelona will have to scrape the barrel to put together teams for their game on a weekend in which the cosmopolitan Spanish league has been badly hit by a mass exodus of players on World Cup duty.

Over forty foreigners will miss league action while Barcelona's three Portuguese internationals will be among half a dozen players facing tight schedules to fly back to Spain in time for their club commitments.
Sixteen countries have exercised their claim on players, with eight Yugoslavians, six Portuguese and five Croatians all answering their countries' calls.
The absence of top stars -- compounded by injuries and suspensions -- even led league-leaders Real Madrid to ask for a postponement of their Sunday evening game at Tenerife.
The request was turned down and Real have been forced to make special arrangements so their Brazilian players can make the trip home for a friendly game.
Barcelona's own leading Brazilian, striker Ronaldo, will take the first plane out after leading his side against Valencia.
Ronaldo scored twice on Wednesday in the 4-0 Cup victory at second division Las Palmas.
But the news was not all good for Barcelona as defender Sergi Barjuan broke his arm in the game, and has further compounded the problems faced by coach Bobby Robson in putting together a side.

Also out are suspended utility man Luis Enrique Martinez, and injured centre-back Abelardo Fernandez, while defender Fernando Couto is unlikely to start the game after flying in from Portugal's game in Northern Ireland.
Couto's compatriot, winger Luis Figo, is in the same boat, but keeper Vitor Baia looks set to play his second game in 24 hours because of a lack of confidence in deputy Carlos Busquets.
Definitely absent is Romanian midfielder Gheorghe Popescu, who will be with his national side.
Valencia, who don't have the spending power or the galaxy of international stars of their Mediterranean rivals, will also have to fill key absences.
Newly-signed playmaker Ariel Ortega will be with Argentina, striker Goran Vlaovic with Croatia and midfielder Valery Karpin with Russia.
Injuries to several other players and the suspension of defender Enrique Romero have further complicated the job faced by coach Jorge Valdano.

Valdano will probably opt to use two men in front of the back four in a bid to stop the defence-splitting through-balls of Ivan de la Pena, who has set up seven goals in as many games since returning to the line-up last month.

De la Pena also hit a superb set-piece goal against Las Palmas and will be anxious to prove himself as a reliable substitute for Brazilian international Giovanni, whose time at Camp Nou seems to be coming to an end after clashes with Robson.
